# voxctrl — programmable voice input broker for Linux & Windows
# llms.txt — structured index for AI agent discovery
# https://llmstxt.org/

> voxctrl transcribes speech entirely on-device using whisper.cpp (CUDA / Vulkan / CPU) or
> Moonshine (streaming ONNX, CPU-native), routes the transcript to named Output Commands
> (inject, clipboard, exec, pipe, socket, file, dbus, http, webhook, mcp, speak, chat, command),
> applies per-command post-processing including rewriting through any OpenAI-compatible API,
> and exposes a built-in MCP server so any MCP-capable agent (Claude, Cursor, Zed) can use the
> microphone and TTS as first-class tools. Nothing is sent anywhere you did not configure.

## Quick Facts

- Version: 0.4.0
- License: MIT
- Platform: Linux (Wayland-native; X11 supported) and Windows 10/11
- Language: Rust (Tauri backend, workspace of 12 crates) + Svelte frontend
- Repository: https://github.com/JRufer/voxctrl
- MCP server: Unix socket /tmp/voxctrl-mcp.sock (Linux), named pipe \\.\pipe\voxctrl-mcp (Windows); JSON-RPC 2.0
- Config: ~/.config/voxctrl/{config.toml, targets.toml, bindings.toml}

## Key Capabilities

1. **First-run setup wizard** — seven steps (welcome, engine, hotkey, overlay, live test, voice, done);
   each choice written to disk as it is made. Reopen with `voxctrl --setup` or Settings → General.
2. **Local transcription** — whisper.cpp (five model sizes, tiny is the default) or Moonshine (tiny, base).
   `engine.whisper_cpp.device = auto|cuda|vulkan|cpu`.
3. **Programmable routing** — 13 delivery types: inject, clipboard, exec, pipe, socket, file, dbus,
   http, webhook, mcp, speak, chat, command.
4. **Voice Command Router** — say "VoxCtrl <command name> <text>" mid-dictation to reroute that
   utterance; natural lead-ins accepted; longest command name wins.
5. **Per-command processing** — remove_fillers, spoken_punctuation, auto_format_lists, code_mode,
   snippets, and LLM rewriting against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
6. **MCP server** — transcribe_voice, speak_text, get_status.
7. **Neural TTS** — Breeze-TTS-2, Pocket-TTS, Piper, Inflect-Micro-v2, eSpeak-NG. All local.
8. **Visual overlays** — eight styles: Ocean Wave (default), Voice Card, Waveform, Pulse Ring,
   Mono Bars, Neon Spectrum, Retro Terminal, Analog VU; or disabled.
9. **Self-updating** — checks GitHub releases on launch, verifies the download against the published
   checksum, replaces itself and restarts. One unauthenticated request; off with one tick in Settings.

## Privacy Model

- Global shortcuts are registered through the XDG GlobalShortcuts portal. voxctrl never reads the
  keyboard; the desktop owns the key grab and reports only that voxctrl's own shortcut fired.
- No udev rule, no `input` group, nothing to grant. Versions before 0.3.3 installed such a rule;
  the installer now removes it if present and never creates it.
- No telemetry, no analytics, no crash reporters. The only self-initiated network request is the
  update check, which carries no identifier and can be turned off.
- Air-gapped ready once models are downloaded.

## MCP Integration

Server name: voxctrl
Socket: /tmp/voxctrl-mcp.sock (Linux) · \\.\pipe\voxctrl-mcp (Windows)
Protocol: JSON-RPC 2.0, newline-delimited

### Tools

| Tool               | Signature                           | Description                                                |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| transcribe_voice   | timeout_seconds?: number → string   | Opens mic, returns transcript after VAD silence or timeout |
| speak_text         | text: string → "spoken"             | Queues text for the configured TTS engine; non-blocking    |
| get_status         | → {recording: bool, speaking: bool} | Returns current audio I/O state                            |

Omit `timeout_seconds` and voxctrl uses the Record timeout from Settings → General (default 15s).

### Claude Desktop config

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "voxctrl": {
      "command": "socat",
      "args": ["STDIO", "UNIX-CONNECT:/tmp/voxctrl-mcp.sock"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Configuration Files

### config.toml (global settings)

Key options: engine.backend, engine.whisper_cpp.model_size, engine.whisper_cpp.device,
engine.moonshine.model_size, tts.engine, tts.hf_token, ui.show_overlay, ui.overlay_style,
ui.overlay_position, audio.vad_threshold, mcp server enable + record timeout, update check on launch.

### targets.toml (Output Commands)

Each [[target]] entry defines: id, label, delivery, optional [target.processing] overrides, and
delivery-specific fields. The file and its [[target]] blocks kept their names when Output Targets
were renamed to Output Commands in 0.4.0.

```toml
[[target]]
id             = "hermes"
label          = "Hermes Agent"
delivery       = "pipe"
pipe_path      = "/tmp/hermes.in"
response_pipe  = "/tmp/hermes.out"
append_newline = true

[hermes.processing]
remove_fillers = true

[[target]]
id       = "cmd_router"
label    = "Voice Command Router"
delivery = "command"
```

### bindings.toml (hotkey gestures)

Each [[binding]] maps keys + gesture to one or more command IDs.
Gesture types: hold | toggle | double_tap | double_tap_hold

```toml
[[binding]]
id         = "dictate_hold"
keys       = ["KEY_LEFTMETA", "KEY_SPACE"]
gesture    = "hold"
target_ids = ["default"]
hold_threshold_ms = 200
```

## Engines

| Engine      | Sizes                                  | Acceleration            | Best for                     |
|-------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------------|------------------------------|
| whisper.cpp | tiny, base, small, medium, large-v3(+turbo) | CUDA / Vulkan / CPU | Accuracy in a quiet room     |
| Moonshine   | tiny, base                             | CPU-native (ONNX)       | Noisy rooms, low latency     |

## TTS Engines

| Engine           | Kind                   | Download            | Notes                                  |
|------------------|------------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Breeze-TTS-2     | neural, expressive     | ~1.2 GB, gated      | Voice Design from a text prompt        |
| Pocket-TTS       | neural, voice cloning  | ~500 MB, gated      | Clones a voice from a reference clip   |
| Piper            | ONNX neural            | ~60 MB per voice    | ~11 voices                             |
| Inflect-Micro-v2 | compact neural (ONNX)  | 38 MB               | Single fixed English voice             |
| eSpeak-NG        | formant synth          | none (bundled)      | Default; always available              |

Gated models need a HuggingFace token with the licence accepted; one token (tts.hf_token) covers both,
and an exported HF_TOKEN takes precedence and is never written to the config.

## Processing Stages

remove_fillers | spoken_punctuation | auto_format_lists | snippets | code_mode | LLM rewrite (OpenAI-compatible)

## Security Model

- Local socket / named pipe only by default; no network exposure.
- No keyboard access: shortcuts arrive through the desktop portal.
- exec delivery spawns with shell=false, so a transcript cannot inject shell syntax.
- webhook delivery signs its POST with HMAC-SHA256 (X-VoxCtrl-Signature).
- Update downloads are verified against the checksum GitHub published before anything is replaced.
